To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) melatonin is a chronobiotic that can be used to treat circadian rhythm sleep disorder (CRSD) patients with delayed sleep onset; (2) melatonin is not effective in treating CRSD patients with advanced sleep onset; (3) light therapy can be used to reset the circadian rhythms of CRSD patients with both delayed and advanced sleep onset; and (4) melatonin and light can be combined to improve the efficacy of therapy in CRSD patients.
melatonin is a hormone that is secreted by the pineal gland in response to the light–dark cycle and is important for the regulation of circadian rhythms.
melatonin is an important mediator of the circadian system and can be used to reset the circadian phase and to promote sleep.

the role of melatonin and its receptor MT1 in circadian rhythm sleep disorder, and we have found that melatonin is an effective treatment for this disorder.

melatonin and light are useful tools in the management of CRSDs, and that their use should be considered in the treatment of patients with these disorders.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of melatonin and/or bright-light therapy in patients with circadian rhythm sleep disorder is a safe, effective and well-tolerated treatment.
the use of melatonin and/or light therapy is effective for treating CRSDs and that these treatments can be combined for better efficacy.
melatonin has a role in the circadian system and that it is useful for treating CRSDs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

exogenous melatonin can be an effective therapy for the treatment of delayed sleep phase syndrome and non-24 h CRSD, whereas the efficacy of melatonin in treating advanced sleep phase syndrome remains to be established.
melatonin and light can be used to treat circadian rhythm disturbances.
melatonin is an effective treatment option for patients with CRSDs, but it is not a panacea for all of these disorders and its effects vary depending on the specific disorder.
